skill.name: terminal-title
skill.description: Updates the terminal window title with an emoji, project name, and current topic during AI coding sessions.
skill.summary: Automatically labels terminal windows with project and topic context.
skill.author: 2389-research

security_audit.summary: I found no malicious code or prompt injection in the audited files. The static findings mostly match Markdown examples, comments, shell syntax, terminal device writes, and control-character sanitizers. The remaining concern is that the skill encourages silent pre-approved local command execution for title updates.

remediation.issue: Silent command execution after permission pre-approval
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the automatic behavior prominently and recommend the narrowest possible allow rules for the bundled title scripts.

remediation.issue: PowerShell execution policy bypass in documentation
remediation.suggestion: Explain why the bypass flag is needed, or remove it when the script can run without bypassing local policy.

remediation.issue: Terminal escape sequence handling depends on sanitization
remediation.suggestion: Keep control-character filtering in both scripts and add tests or documentation for ANSI injection prevention.

semantic_findings.title: Silent Pre-Approved Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill asks users to pre-approve shell permissions, then instructs the agent to execute the title update silently and continue without mentioning it. The command is limited to terminal-title scripts, but the behavior should be clearly disclosed because it reduces per-run visibility.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The prose explicitly requests permission pre-approval and silent execution. The audited scripts appear limited and sanitized, so the finding is about user visibility rather than malicious payload behavior.

content.value_statement: Terminal windows become hard to identify during long coding sessions. This skill updates titles with project and topic context across Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
actual_capabilities: Updates terminal titles using emoji, project name, and current topic.
Provides Bash and PowerShell scripts for Unix-like systems and Windows.
Reads TERMINAL_TITLE_EMOJI with a fallback emoji.
Removes control characters and truncates project and topic values.
Documents title updates at session start and topic changes.
limitations: Requires permission to run local shell or PowerShell scripts.
Only changes the terminal title; it does not manage tabs or windows.
Project detection depends on the agent context and may need correction.
Terminal escape sequence support varies by terminal emulator.

use_cases.description: Show the current project name in each terminal during multi-repository work.

use_cases.title: Label Debugging Sessions
use_cases.description: Update titles when a conversation shifts from planning to debugging or testing.

use_cases.title: Standardize Pairing Workflows
use_cases.description: Keep shared terminal sessions labeled with clear project and topic names.

prompt_templates.title: Set Current Title
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the terminal title for this session using the current project and topic.

prompt_templates.title: Name This Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Detect a human-friendly project name from the current repository, then update the terminal title.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh After Topic Change
prompt_templates.prompt: The topic changed to testing. Update the terminal title with the current project and testing topic.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Title Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current repository context, detect whether the topic changed, and update the title only if needed.

output_examples.output: The terminal title becomes a work emoji, Billing API, and Claude Code.

output_examples.input: The conversation shifts from frontend styling to database migrations.
output_examples.output: The terminal title changes to the project name and Database Migrations.

best_practices: Keep project names short and recognizable.
Use concise topic labels that describe the active work.
Review shell permissions before enabling automatic title updates.
anti_patterns: Do not use long sentences as terminal topics.
Do not grant broader shell permissions than the bundled scripts need.
Do not rely on title updates for security or access control.

faq.question: What does this skill change?
faq.answer: It changes the terminal window title to show an emoji, project name, and current topic.

faq.question: Does it read project files?
faq.answer: The instructions ask the agent to infer project context, but the scripts only receive text arguments.

faq.question: Does it send data over the network?
faq.answer: No network behavior was found in the audited files.

faq.question: Why does it need shell permission?
faq.answer: It runs a local script that emits a terminal escape sequence to set the title.

faq.question: Can I choose the emoji?
faq.answer: Yes. Set TERMINAL_TITLE_EMOJI before running the skill, or use the default fallback emoji.

faq.question: Which platforms are supported?
faq.answer: The skill includes Bash support for Unix-like systems and PowerShell support for Windows.
